hero.h1: Make sense of your iPhone App Privacy Report.

product.body: Apple’s report records data and sensor access alongside network contacts. Privacy Score helps you explore those domains and their classifications. A contact is not proof of a leak: this report does not reveal encrypted request contents.
bullets: Import through Apple’s report sharing menu.
Analyze the file on your device.
Compare reports in your score history.

steps.title: Enable Apple’s report
steps.body: Open Settings → Privacy & Security → App Privacy Report. Enable it if needed, then use your apps to collect activity.

steps.title: Share the report
steps.body: Use the iOS report’s share or save option, then open the file with Privacy Score. The file is analyzed on your device.

steps.title: Choose your next steps
steps.body: Review domains and recommendations. Adjust permissions for your needs; the score is an internal indicator, not a security guarantee.

cards.title: An explained indicator

cards.title: Visible limits
cards.body: The report describes observed activity. It does not expose TLS contents or cover every part of your usage.

faq.title: What to know before your first audit.

items.a: Data and sensor access, plus domains contacted by apps and websites during the recorded period. It does not reveal request contents. See Apple’s documentation.

Yes. Your first audit is free. Premium includes additional audits, DNS/VPN tools and export. In the French App Store, the annual launch offer is €23.88 for the first year, then €59.99/year at the current price, for eligible subscriptions. Apple confirms local pricing and terms before purchase.

items.q: What if my report is empty?
items.a: Recording starts after you enable it. Use your apps and check again. Do not turn the report off to refresh it: that clears recorded data. Read the troubleshooting guide.

items.q: Does a contacted domain prove tracking?
items.a: No. A connection can support content, authentication, notifications or measurement. Consider the domain, its context and the limits of its classification before drawing a conclusion.
Privacy Score is available for iPhone and iPad running iOS/iPadOS 17.6 or later. The app and website support English and French. Check the App Store listing for your device’s compatibility.
